children: Raw sugar futures on ICE fell sharply on Thursday, retreating from the previous session's 19-month high, as investors viewed the latest El Nino-inspired rally that took prices well above 20 cents as overdone, while coffee also fell.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
settled down 0.68 cent, or 3.3%, at 20.15 cents per lb, after setting a 19-month high of 21.24 cents on Wednesday.
* "The market appears to have gotten overdone on the El Nino-inspired production worries," said broker ADMIS.
* Heavy El Nino-linked rains, which have disrupted harvest and crushing activity in top grower Brazil, are expected to persist over the next week, according to forecasters.
* The El Nino weather event is also expected to curb sugar  production in Asia this season.
* The US Department of Agriculture revised downward its sugar production estimates for both Brazil and India due to El Nino impacts.
* In news, Europe's Sudzucker
said it expects EU sugar prices to rebound from their recent four-year lows as droughts and low rainfall take a toll on beet harvests.
* White sugar
​fell 2.6% to $541.10 a metric ton.
COFFEE
* Arabica coffee
settled down 3.65 cents, or 1.2%, at $2.8905 per lb​​, having closed down 3.9% on Wednesday.
* Arabica is under pressure from surging exports from top grower Brazil.
* Brazil's September green coffee exports were the highest  in 20 months, data showed.
* However, concerns the El Nino weather event will curb global output in 2027/28 are underpinning prices.
* As a case in point, premiums for Central American arabica have risen to their highest in around three years amid an El Nino-linked drought.
* Robusta coffee
lost 1.8% to $3,423 a ton.
COCOA
* London cocoa
settled up £59, or 1.4%, to £4,233  per ton.
* "The 2025/26 surplus continues to grow, with estimates putting it between 450,000 and 720,000 tons. This would be the largest surplus we have ever seen," broker StoneX said in a note.
* It added, however, that forecasts for 2026/27 vary between a wide deficit and a surplus, with the main point of uncertainty being the effect El Nino will have on crops.

* In news, the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) has secured 3.39 billion cedis ($288.02 million) through the issue of short-term debt on the domestic market, funding that should allow the regulator to boost purchases from farmers.
* New York cocoa
rose 1.5% to $5,665 a ton.
